items.title: International Debate Webinar: Eastern and Western Medicine Can Co-exist – part of London Global Cancer Week 2026
items.summary: Monday 2 November 2026 | 21:00 GMT (check your local time) Part of London Global Cancer Week 2026 Can Eastern and Western medicine co-exist in modern cancer care?

items.title: Cervical cancer screening – a practical guide for nurses in primary care
items.summary: Lead nurse at The Eve Appeal charity Helen Hyndman explains the key principles and practical steps involved in the national cervical cancer screening programme, and how nurses in primary care can support with improving uptake. Read the full CPD module on Nursing in Practice 365 today.

items.title: Impact of staff training on body temperature measurements during cancer treatment: a single-site quality improvement project
items.summary: Background: Neutropenic sepsis is a serious complication of cancer therapy, and can often be detected by the presence of abnormal body temperature, typically fever. Aims: This research aimed to improve home temperature measurement in a cancer triage unit following a previous audit.

items.title: BOPA 2026 Mentioned in Pharmaceutical Journal
items.summary: Invest in aseptic services for future of specialised medicines, says chief pharmacist – The Pharmaceutical Journal Aseptic facilities are “absolutely essential” for hospitals to be involved in clinical trials…

items.title: Implementation and evaluation of a nurse-led clinic for men referred with suspected prostate cancer
items.summary: Background: Cancer diagnostic delays remain a challenge. Advanced nurse-led clinics represent an innovative approach to improving pathway efficiency while delivering person-centred care.

items.title: Nurse teams up with researchers on breast cancer drug study
items.summary: Find out more about a specialist nurse in Somerset who has teamed up with a team of researchers to help with a study on the side effects of a breast cancer medication.

items.title: Framework for the Provision of Dose Banded Products & Patient Specific Chemotherapy Services
items.summary: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust. The East Midlands Pharmacy Collaborative (EMPC) as the Authority wishes to establish a multi-provider Framework Agreement for its members the Dose Banded Products & Patient Specific Chemotherapy Services as defined in this specification.

items.title: GIRFT launches national radiotherapy workstream to cut 31-day treatment delays
items.summary: GIRFT has started a radiotherapy workstream supporting the 85% 62-day cancer target.

items.title: Cancer Vaccines: “Transforming Vaccine Delivery Through Innovation”
items.summary: Session Title: Cancer Vaccines: “Transforming Vaccine Delivery Through Innovation” When: 12th October 2026.

items.title: Urine test could speed up bladder cancer diagnosis in patients with haematuria
items.summary: A non-invasive urine test could speed up diagnosis of bladder cancer, an NHS study has found. Trials of the GALEAS urine bladder test across seven NHS sites found it discovered nine in ten patients with the disease.

items.title: Womb cancer tests could be used in primary care
items.summary: A test to rule out womb cancer in women who experience bleeding after menopause could be used in primary care, a study has found. The University of Manchester study found that the test – which uses urine and vaginal fluid – correctly identified more than 80% of cancers and achieved a negative predictive value of...

items.title: Xiel supplies MVision AI radiotherapy contouring platform to Cambridge University Hospitals
items.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust has signed a one-year, £15,000 contract with medical technology distributor Xiel Ltd for the MVision AI platform, a radiotherapy-focused artificial intelligence tool that automatically generates anatomical contours from CT and MR images to…

items.title: NICE approves life-extending treatment for advanced breast cancer
items.summary: Around 1,000 women in England with advanced breast cancer can now receive life-extending treatment, under guidance for the health service from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE).

items.title: Life-extending breast cancer drug approved for NHS following price deal
items.summary: NICE has finally recommended the life-extending breast cancer drug Enhertu for routine NHS use after reaching a new commercial arrangement.

items.title: Nurses at forefront of awareness campaign for rare women’s cancer
items.summary: Nurses at the South Eastern Trust are encouraging women to be vigilant about the signs and symptoms of vulval and vaginal cancer and to seek medical advice if they notice any changes.

items.title: Suspected cancer among 44k ‘rejected referral’ letters never sent to GPs
items.summary: Health officials in Northern Ireland are investigating whether any patients have come to harm, as an issue with undelivered letters from hospitals to GPs was revealed be of a much greater scale than initially thought.

items.title: Structured exercise programmes ‘improve’ cancer survival
items.summary: Structured exercise programmes for people with cancer can help them live longer and extend the amount of time that they live cancer-free, according to new research.
